claim: IL-2 is produced in a binary (digital or all-or-none) manner by Th cells in vitro.
source: Previously, we showed in vitro that IL-2 is produced in a binary ('digital' or 'all-or-none') manner by Th cells (Podtschaske et al., 2007), because variation of strength of the stimulation changed the number of IL-2 expressing cells rather than the intensity of IL-2 per cell.
evidence: Supported by citation to Podtschaske et al., 2007 and described experimental observation

claim: Different amounts of antigen used for immunization result in changes in the number of IL-2-producing cells but almost no change in the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) of IL-2 expression per Th cell in vivo.
source: Different amounts of antigen used for immunization resulted in changes in the number of IL-2-producing cells (Figure 1A, left), but almost no change in the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) of IL-2 expression per Th cell (Figure 1A, right).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A

claim: The amount of antigen correlates with the proportion of Th cells that produced IL-2, but does not change the amount of IL-2 per cell.
source: Thus, the amount of antigen correlates with the proportion of Th cells that produced IL-2, but does not change the amount of IL-2 per cell, which confirms that IL-2 production is regulated in a binary fashion in vivo, too.
evidence: Inference from experimental data showing correlation between antigen amount and IL-2+ cell frequency

claim: IL-2 production is regulated in a binary fashion in vivo.
source: Thus, the amount of antigen correlates with the proportion of Th cells that produced IL-2, but does not change the amount of IL-2 per cell, which confirms that IL-2 production is regulated in a binary fashion in vivo, too.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data on antigen dose-dependent IL-2 production

claim: IL-2 expression peaks between 6 and 18 hr after immunization.
source: The IL-2 expression peaked between 6 and 18 hr (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by time-course experimental data shown in Figure 1D

claim: The IL-2 secretion assay detected up to 75% IL-2-producing Th cells at the highest amount of antigen (2 mg).
source: The IL-2 secretion assay detected up to 75% IL-2-producing Th cells at the highest amount of antigen (2 mg) used.
evidence: Direct measurement from IL-2 secretion assay experiments

claim: Direct measurement of IL-2 by intracellular staining only detected maximally ~9% IL-2-producing Th cells.
source: This number reflects the in vivo situation better than direct measurement of IL-2 by intracellular staining, which only detected maximally ~9% IL-2-producing Th cells, considered to be too low (Long and Adler, 2006).
evidence: Comparison of experimental methods with citation to Long and Adler, 2006

claim: CD25 expression is graded in vivo at both single cell and population level.
source: Interestingly, unlike IL-2, and in contrast to some in vitro data, CD25 and CD69 expression is clearly graded in vivo at both, single cell and population level (Figure 1B,C) (Feinerman et al., 2010; Tkach et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 1B,C and contrasted with cited in vitro studies

claim: CD69 expression is graded in vivo at both single cell and population level.
source: Interestingly, unlike IL-2, and in contrast to some in vitro data, CD25 and CD69 expression is clearly graded in vivo at both, single cell and population level (Figure 1B,C) (Feinerman et al., 2010; Tkach et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 1B,C and contrasted with cited in vitro studies

claim: Different antigen concentrations change the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) of CD25 expression per Th cell.
source: Different antigen concentrations used for immunization changed the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) of CD25 expression per Th cell (Figure 1B, right).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B

claim: The amount of antigen correlates with the amount of CD25 expressed per cell.
source: The amount of antigen correlated with the amount of CD25 expressed per cell (Figure 1B, left), and thus its ability to respond to IL-2.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B

claim: CD25 expression was up-regulated only by transferred antigen-specific Th and Treg cells, but not by endogenous T cells.
source: Notably, CD25 expression was up-regulated only by transferred antigen-specific Th and Treg cells (Figure 1—figure supplements 5A and 6), but not by endogenous T cells.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 5A and 6

claim: CD25 expression is preferentially up-regulated via TCR-stimulated T cell activation.
source: This fact is pointing to preferential up-regulation of CD25 expression via TCR-stimulated T cell activation.
evidence: Inference from observation that only antigen-specific cells upregulate CD25

claim: High expression of CD69 is observed only on antigen-specific T cells.
source: The same holds true for high expression of CD69 (Figure 1—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5B

claim: A small bystander expression of CD69 (CD69intermediate cells) was observed on endogenous Th and Treg cells after immunization of mice with OVA + LPS.
source: However, a small bystander expression of CD69 (CD69intermediate cells) was observed on endogenous Th and Treg cells after immunization of mice with OVA + LPS.
evidence: Observation from experimental data on CD69 expression

claim: Both IL-2 secretion and CD25 expression reach their maximum value between 3 to 6 hr after immunization.
source: Both processes reached their maximum value between 3 to 6 hr and obviously CD25 protein expression persisted longer than IL-2 secretion.
evidence: Supported by kinetics data shown in Figure 1D

claim: CD25 protein expression persists longer than IL-2 secretion.
source: Both processes reached their maximum value between 3 to 6 hr and obviously CD25 protein expression persisted longer than IL-2 secretion.
evidence: Observation from time-course experimental data

claim: The amount and variation of CD25 expression is similar in IL-2-producing and IL-2-nonproducing cells 14 hr after immunization with different antigen concentrations.
source: Interestingly, co-staining of CD25 and IL-2 in adoptively transferred transgenic Th cells (Figure 2A, top row) revealed that the amount and variation of CD25 expression is similar in IL-2-producing and IL-2-nonproducing cells 14 hr after immunization with different antigen concentrations (Figure 2A, bottom row).
evidence: Supported by co-staining experimental data shown in Figure 2A

claim: The kinetics of IL-2 secretion and CD25 expression was similar in IL-2-producing and IL-2-nonproducing cells during the time of expression of both molecules.
source: Accordingly, the kinetics of IL-2 secretion and CD25 expression in adoptively transferred transgenic Th cells after immunization of mice with 2 mg OVA + 10 µg LPS was similar in IL-2-producing and IL-2-nonproducing cells during the time of expression of both molecules (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by kinetics data shown in Figure 2B

claim: Mainly the amount of antigen and a paracrine, rather than an autocrine, action of IL-2 regulates the expression of CD25 in vivo.
source: These data suggest that mainly the amount of antigen and a paracrine, rather than an autocrine, action of IL-2 regulates the expression of CD25 in vivo.
evidence: Inference from observation that IL-2+ and IL-2- cells have similar CD25 expression

claim: Only the amount of c-Fos but not of NFATc2 per Th cell correlates with the probability of IL-2 expression in vivo.
source: Interestingly, only the amount of c-Fos but not of NFATc2 per Th cell correlates with the probability of IL-2 expression in vivo.
evidence: Supported by co-staining experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: The probability of IL-2 production correlates with the c-Fos amount per cell but is independent of NFATc2 amounts within their physiological range.
source: Quartiles with the same cell number but different fluorescence intensities of c-Fos or NFATc2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4, left) showed that the probability of IL-2 production correlates with the c-Fos amount per cell but is independent of NFATc2 amounts within their physiological range (Figure 1—figure supplement 4, right).
evidence: Supported by quartile analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: The MEK/ERK/AP1 axis plays an important role in translating TCR signaling into proportional activation of genes essential for T cell function.
source: This is in line with the observation of Allison et al. that the MEK/ERK/AP1 axis plays an important role in translating TCR signaling into proportional activation of genes essential for T cell function (Allison et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Allison et al., 2016

claim: CD25 expression peaks between 12 and 24 hr after immunization.
source: Given that CD25 expression peaks between 12 and 24 hr after immunization (Lischke et al., 2012; Long and Adler, 2006), we observed graded CD25 and CD69 expression of adoptively transferred transgenic CD4+ T cells 14 hr after immunization of mice.
evidence: Supported by citations to Lischke et al., 2012 and Long and Adler, 2006

claim: Binary IL-2 and graded CD25 expression as well as higher CD25 expression by Treg cells ensures a fast action and wide linear antigen response range of Treg cells.
source: In summary, binary IL-2 and graded CD25 expression as well as higher CD25 expression by Treg cells ensures a fast action and wide linear antigen response range of Treg cells.
evidence: Summary conclusion from computational modeling results

claim: The model simulations predict that Th cells are activated at lower antigen concentrations in the binary than in the graded scenario.
source: Interestingly, the model simulations predict that Th cells are activated at lower antigen concentrations in the binary than in the graded scenario.
evidence: Prediction from computational model simulations

claim: Treg cells are always activated at lower antigen concentrations than Th cells.
source: However, Treg cells are always activated at lower antigen concentrations than Th cells.
evidence: Conclusion from computational model and experimental data

claim: With increasing amounts of antigen (and hence increasing IL-2 secretion) STAT5 phosphorylation increases proportionally in antigen-specific Th and Treg cells.
source: As expected, with increasing amounts of antigen (and hence increasing IL-2 secretion) STAT5 phosphorylation increased proportionally in antigen-specific Th and Treg cells.
evidence: Supported by p-STAT5 staining data shown in Figure 3C

claim: Antigen-specific Treg cells show much higher STAT5 phosphorylation than antigen-specific Th cells.
source: Moreover, antigen-specific Treg cells showed a much higher STAT5 phosphorylation than antigen-specific Th cells.
evidence: Supported by p-STAT5 staining data shown in Figure 3C

claim: At the highest antigen concentration (2 mg OVA) only ~11% of Th cells stained positive for p-STAT5 despite the fact that about 75% of Th cells secrete IL-2 and about 95% express CD25.
source: Even at the highest antigen concentration (2 mg OVA) only ~11% of Th cells stained positive for p-STAT5 despite the fact that about 75% of Th cells secrete IL-2 and about 95% express CD25 at this condition (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by p-STAT5 staining data shown in Figure 3C

claim: Within the Treg cell population about 50% were p-STAT5+ at the highest antigen concentration.
source: Within the Treg cell population about 50% were p-STAT5+ (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by p-STAT5 staining data shown in Figure 3C

claim: The induction of p-STAT5 is lower in naïve Th cells compared to repeatedly activated cells but lasts longer.
source: O' Gorman et al. described that the induction of p-STAT5 is lower in naïve Th cells compared to repeatedly activated cells but lasts longer (O'Gorman et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to O'Gorman et al., 2009

claim: Endogenous antigen-unspecific Th cells have very low expression of CD25 and almost no p-STAT5.
source: In line with this, our endogenous antigen-unspecific Th cells had a very low expression of CD25 and almost no p-STAT5.
evidence: Observation from experimental data on endogenous T cells

claim: STAT5 activation was observed at a similar degree on both transgenic (antigen-specific) and endogenous Treg cell populations.
source: In contrast, STAT5 activation (Figure 3C) was observed at a similar degree on both Treg cell populations, transgenic (antigen-specific) and endogenous Treg cells.
evidence: Supported by p-STAT5 staining data shown in Figure 3C

claim: Neither IL-2 treatment of mice nor in vitro IL-2 treatment of Th cells increased STAT5 activation in transgenic Th cells.
source: The data clearly show that neither IL-2 treatment of mice nor in vitro IL-2 treatment of Th cells increased STAT5 activation in transgenic Th cells (Figure 4).
evidence: Supported by IL-2 treatment experimental data shown in Figure 4

claim: Antigen-specific Th cells are unresponsive to IL-2 by negative crosstalk between antigen and IL-2 signaling.
source: Thus it is very probable that antigen-specific Th cells are unresponsive to IL-2 by negative crosstalk between antigen and IL-2 signaling as described before (Tkach et al., 2014; Villarino et al., 2007; Waysbort et al., 2013).
evidence: Inference from experimental data with support from cited literature

claim: At low amounts of antigen (<30 µg OVA) preferentially a proportion of Treg cells is activated by IL-2.
source: First, at low amounts of antigen (<30 µg OVA) preferentially a proportion of Treg cells is activated by IL-2, and thus can limit the immune response at low danger.
evidence: Conclusion from model and experimental data

claim: Binary IL-2 expression tailors the fraction of activated Treg cells proportionately to the antigen amount.
source: Second, binary IL-2 expression tailors the fraction of activated Treg cells proportionately to the antigen amount and avoids that all Treg cells are almost simultaneously activated as would be expected in the graded IL-2 expression scenario.
evidence: Conclusion from computational modeling and experimental data

claim: At low antigen amounts binary IL-2 expression ensures by its spatial distribution that only those antigen-specific and unspecific Treg cells are activated which are in close spatial proximity to the few IL-2 producing Th cells.
source: Third, at low antigen amounts binary IL-2 expression ensures by its spatial distribution that only those antigen-specific and unspecific Treg cells are activated, which are in close spatial proximity to the few IL-2 producing Th cells.
evidence: Conclusion from computational modeling with support from cited literature

claim: Antigen-specific Th and Treg cells did not proliferate after immunization at low antigen concentrations (2–8 µg OVA) in CFSE dilution assays.
source: Using the adoptive transfer model, we found that antigen-specific Th and Treg cells did not proliferate after immunization at low antigen concentrations (2–8 µg OVA) in CFSE dilution assays (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by CFSE dilution experimental data shown in Figure 5A

claim: At low antigen concentrations (2-8 µg OVA), similar total cell counts and relative frequencies were observed as in the unimmunized controls.
source: In line with this, we observed similar total cell counts and relative frequencies as in the unimmunized controls under these conditions (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: Supported by cell count data shown in Figure 5B,C

claim: The percentage of dividing progenitors was approximately 10%, which appeared to be the background level already present in Th and Treg cells without immunization.
source: The percentage of dividing progenitors was approximately 10%, which appeared to be the background level already present in Th and Treg cells without immunization (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 5D

claim: Above 8 µg OVA, total cell numbers of transgenic Th and Treg cells increased proportionally to the antigen amount, but with a dramatically different slope.
source: Above 8 µg OVA, total cell numbers of transgenic Th and Treg cells increased proportionally to the antigen amount, but with a dramatic different slope.
evidence: Observation from cell count data shown in Figure 5B

claim: CFSE dilution profiles revealed a stronger proliferative response of OVA-specific Th cells compared to Treg cells at higher concentrations.
source: CFSE dilution profiles revealed a stronger proliferative response of OVA-specific Th cells compared to Treg cells at higher concentrations.
evidence: Observation from CFSE dilution data shown in Figure 5

claim: At 500 µg OVA, 94% of Th cell progenitors were dividing compared to 65% of Treg cell progenitors.
source: As an example, at 500 µg OVA 94% of Th cell progenitors were dividing compared to 65% of Treg cell progenitors (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 5D

claim: Antigen-specific Treg cells showed less apoptosis than antigen-specific Th cells, in particular at low antigen concentrations (4–5% and 7–9% apoptotic cells, respectively, at 2–8 µg OVA).
source: In both assays, antigen-specific Treg cells showed less apoptosis than antigen-specific Th cells, in particular at low antigen concentrations (4–5% and 7–9% apoptotic cells, respectively, at 2–8 µg OVA).
evidence: Supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: Apoptosis of Treg cells was proportionally increasing with the antigen amount up to the level of Th cells at 2000 µg OVA.
source: Apoptosis of Treg cells was proportionally increasing with the antigen amount up to the level of Th cells at 2000 µg OVA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: The apoptosis rate of antigen-specific Th cells was almost constant over the covered antigen concentration range.
source: In contrast, the apoptosis rate of antigen-specific Th cells was almost constant over the covered antigen concentration range.
evidence: Observation from apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: At low antigen concentrations (2–8 µg OVA), apoptosis does not play an important role because T cell numbers were only slightly reduced at 72 hr.
source: Comparing cell counts at low antigen concentrations (2–8 µg OVA) (left parts of Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), it is obvious that apoptosis does not play an important role because T cell numbers were only slightly reduced at 72 hr.
evidence: Inference from comparison of cell count and apoptosis data

claim: At higher antigen concentrations (>8 µg OVA) the cells expand proportionately to the antigen load, but living antigen-specific Th expand more than Treg cells.
source: At higher concentrations (>8 µg OVA) the cells expand proportionately to the antigen load, but it is obvious that living antigen-specific Th expand more than Treg cells (Figure 5B–D), which is in contrast to a previous report using IL-2 reporter mice (Amado et al., 2013).
evidence: Observation from proliferation data with contrast to cited literature

claim: IL-2 is mainly produced by activated Foxp3− CD4+ T helper cells.
source: IL-2 is mainly produced by activated Foxp3− CD4+ T helper cells (hereinafter referred to as 'Th cells') and mediates diverse pleiotropic actions such as promotion of Th1 and Th2 differentiation, expansion of multiple Th cell populations, as well as generation and maintenance of Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (Treg cells) (Liao et al., 2013).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by citation to Liao et al., 2013

claim: IL-2 mediates diverse pleiotropic actions such as promotion of Th1 and Th2 differentiation, expansion of multiple Th cell populations, as well as generation and maintenance of Foxp3+ regulatory T cells.
source: IL-2 is mainly produced by activated Foxp3− CD4+ T helper cells (hereinafter referred to as 'Th cells') and mediates diverse pleiotropic actions such as promotion of Th1 and Th2 differentiation, expansion of multiple Th cell populations, as well as generation and maintenance of Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (Treg cells) (Liao et al., 2013).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by citation to Liao et al., 2013

claim: IL-2 positively acts on Th cells through synergistic effects between antigen and cytokines and negatively through preferred binding to and activation of Foxp3+ Treg cells.
source: Thus, IL-2 positively acts on Th cells through synergistic effects between antigen and cytokines and negatively through preferred binding to and activation of Foxp3+ Treg cells.
evidence: Summary of established IL-2 biology

claim: Individual T cells sense both antigen affinity and frequency and tailor the collective antigen-specific T cell activation to the antigen amount.
source: Individual T cells sense both antigen affinity and frequency and tailor the collective antigen-specific T cell activation to the antigen amount (Allison et al., 2016; Gottschalk et al., 2012; Kellogg et al., 2015; Miskov-Zivanov et al., 2013).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by multiple citations

claim: Sojka et al. studied the kinetics of IL-2 secretion by naive and memory Th cells.
source: First, Sojka et al. studied the kinetics of IL-2 secretion by naive and memory Th cells (Sojka et al., 2004) and some studies observed a paracrine IL-2 action on STAT5 activation (Long and Adler, 2006; O'Gorman et al., 2009; Sabatos et al., 2008).
evidence: Citation to prior work by Sojka et al., 2004

claim: Some studies observed a paracrine IL-2 action on STAT5 activation.
source: First, Sojka et al. studied the kinetics of IL-2 secretion by naive and memory Th cells (Sojka et al., 2004) and some studies observed a paracrine IL-2 action on STAT5 activation (Long and Adler, 2006; O'Gorman et al., 2009; Sabatos et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Long and Adler, 2006; O'Gorman et al., 2009; Sabatos et al., 2008

claim: Amado et al. proposed that IL-2 is sensed by both the activated Th cell pool and by Treg cells, which reciprocally regulate cells of the IL-2-producing cell subset in IL-2 reporter mice.
source: Second, Amado et al. proposed that IL-2 is sensed by both the activated Th cell pool and by Treg cells, which reciprocally regulate cells of the IL-2-producing cell subset in IL-2 reporter mice (Amado et al., 2013).
evidence: Citation to prior work by Amado et al., 2013

claim: O'Gorman et al. showed that in the initial phase of antigen-specific activation IL-2-dependent STAT5 phosphorylation occurred primarily in Treg cells.
source: Third, O'Gorman et al. showed that in the initial phase of antigen-specific activation IL-2-dependent STAT5 phosphorylation occurred primarily in Treg cells (O'Gorman et al., 2009).
evidence: Citation to prior work by O'Gorman et al., 2009

claim: Liu et al. underscored the importance of a fine-tuned local IL-2 availability to limit otherwise constant damage from activated auto-responsive Th cells under steady state conditions.
source: Fourth, Liu et al. underscored the importance of a fine-tuned local IL-2 availability to limit otherwise constant damage from activated auto-responsive Th cells under steady state conditions (Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: Citation to prior work by Liu et al., 2015

claim: Binary responses are able to filter out noisy signals and can integrate different information to control cell responses.
source: This is an interesting issue because binary responses are able to filter out noisy signals and can integrate different information to control cell responses.
evidence: General principle about binary responses

claim: Binary responses allow parallel and independent control of single cell activation probability and population heterogeneity.
source: Thereby, binary responses allow parallel and independent control of single cell activation probability and population heterogeneity (Kellogg et al., 2015; Köck et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kellogg et al., 2015 and Köck et al., 2014

claim: In the binary scenario for IL-2, the number of activated Th and Treg cells slowly increases with increasing antigen stimulus.
source: Our simulations show that in the binary scenario for IL-2 the number of activated Th and Treg cells slowly increases with increasing antigen stimulus, while the behaviour is rather switch-like in the graded case (Figure 3B).
evidence: Result from computational model simulations shown in Figure 3B

claim: In the graded IL-2 scenario, the behavior of activated Th and Treg cells is rather switch-like.
source: Our simulations show that in the binary scenario for IL-2 the number of activated Th and Treg cells slowly increases with increasing antigen stimulus, while the behaviour is rather switch-like in the graded case (Figure 3B).
evidence: Result from computational model simulations shown in Figure 3B

claim: If secretion is graded, the distribution of IL-2 is relatively homogeneous across the whole volume.
source: This can be understood in the following way: If secretion is graded (i.e. many producers), the distribution of IL-2 is relatively homogeneous across the whole volume.
evidence: Explanation of computational model behavior

claim: In the graded IL-2 scenario, all cells are exposed to similar levels of IL-2 and thus are either all activated or not.
source: Consequently, all cells are exposed to similar levels of IL-2 and thus are either all activated or not in the graded IL-2 scenario.
evidence: Explanation of computational model behavior

claim: If secretion is binary, the number of activated cells increases more gradually because cells that are in close proximity to secreting cells are activated first.
source: If secretion is binary (i.e. the number of secreting cells increases with increasing stimulus, the amount is constant), by contrast, then the number of activated cells increases more gradually because cells that are in close proximity to secreting cells are activated first.
evidence: Explanation of computational model behavior

claim: Binary secretion at the cellular level leads to graded activation at the population level and vice versa.
source: Binary secretion at the cellular level thus leads to graded activation at the population level and vice versa.
evidence: Conclusion from computational model analysis

claim: Binding of IL-2 influences CD25 expression in Th cells.
source: Binding of IL-2 influences CD25 expression in Th cells as shown by several groups using single cell in vitro experiments including mathematical modeling (Busse et al., 2010; Feinerman et al., 2008; Tkach et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple in vitro studies

claim: IL-2 enhances TCR-induced up-regulation of CD25 level at suboptimal stimulation.
source: IL-2 enhances TCR-induced up-regulation of CD25 level at suboptimal stimulation (Feinerman et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Feinerman et al., 2008

claim: IL-2 is delivered to neighboring T cells via synapses.
source: These data are consistent with previous reports showing via STAT5 activation that IL-2 is delivered to neighboring T cells via synapses (Sabatos et al., 2008) and that IL-2 production does not coincide with STAT5 phosphorylation (Long and Adler, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sabatos et al., 2008

claim: IL-2 production does not coincide with STAT5 phosphorylation.
source: These data are consistent with previous reports showing via STAT5 activation that IL-2 is delivered to neighboring T cells via synapses (Sabatos et al., 2008) and that IL-2 production does not coincide with STAT5 phosphorylation (Long and Adler, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Long and Adler, 2006

claim: IL-2 expression precedes CD25 expression in vivo.
source: The observed peak times of IL-2 (6–14 hr) and CD25 (12–24 hr) show that IL-2 expression precedes CD25 expression in vivo, which is in good agreement with previous observations (Lischke et al., 2012; Long and Adler, 2006).
evidence: Inference from kinetics data with support from cited literature

claim: IL-2 from strongly activated clones co-opt a fraction of weaker clones into activation and proliferation.
source: First, weaker T cell clones can be activated and proliferate just by integrating antigen and IL-2 response. Thus, IL-2 from strongly activated clones co-opt a fraction of weaker clones into activation and proliferation (Voisinne et al., 2015) and contribute thereby to continuous heterogeneity of the responding population.
evidence: Supported by citation to Voisinne et al., 2015

claim: IL-2 may act as a gatekeeper for T cell homeostasis during an immune response, initiating the down-modulation of excessive or boosting of weak effector T cell responses by the interplay of Th and Treg cells.
source: Second, IL-2 may act as a gatekeeper for T cell homeostasis during an immune response, initiating the down-modulation of excessive or boosting of weak effector T cell responses by the interplay of Th and Treg cells (Almeida et al., 2012, 2006; Amado et al., 2013; Reynolds et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: The combination of binary IL-2 secretion and graded CD25 expression at the cellular level enables the parallel control of single cell activation probability and population heterogeneity by the respective antigen amount.
source: Finally, our results demonstrate that the combination of binary IL-2 secretion and graded CD25 expression at the cellular level enables the parallel control of single cell activation probability and population heterogeneity by the respective antigen amount.
evidence: Main conclusion from combined experimental and modeling results

claim: Only binary IL-2 expression ensures a wide linear antigen response range for Teff and Treg cells under real spatiotemporal conditions.
source: Combining in vivo data with a mathematical model we demonstrate that only this binary IL-2 expression ensures a wide linear antigen response range for Teff and Treg cells under real spatiotemporal conditions.
evidence: Main conclusion from combined experimental and modeling results stated in abstract

claim: At low antigen concentrations binary IL-2 expression safeguards by its spatial distribution selective STAT5 activation only of closely adjacent Treg cells regardless of their antigen specificity.
source: Furthermore, at low antigen concentrations binary IL-2 expression safeguards by its spatial distribution selective STAT5 activation only of closely adjacent Treg cells regardless of their antigen specificity.
evidence: Main conclusion from combined experimental and modeling results stated in abstract

claim: The mode of IL-2 secretion is critical to tailor the adaptive immune response to the antigen amount.
source: These data show that the mode of IL-2 secretion is critical to tailor the adaptive immune response to the antigen amount.
evidence: Main conclusion stated in abstract

claim: At single cell level, IL-2 is binary (digital) and CD25 is graded expressed whereas at population level both parameters show graded expression correlating with the antigen amount.
source: Here we find that at single cell level, IL-2 is binary (digital) and CD25 is graded expressed whereas at population level both parameters show graded expression correlating with the antigen amount.
evidence: Main finding stated in abstract

claim: Liu et al. discovered that STAT5 was phosphorylated in most clustering Treg cells and that an IL-2-producing Th cell was usually at the center of Treg cell clusters.
source: Recently, Liu et al. provided information on how the spatial organization of IL-2-producing Th cells and activated Treg cells might help to maintain immune homeostasis (Liu et al., 2015). Using imaging flow cytometry (histo-cytometry) they discovered that STAT5 was phosphorylated in most clustering Treg cells and that an IL-2-producing Th cell was usually at the center of Treg cell clusters.
evidence: Citation to prior work by Liu et al., 2015

claim: The reduction of motility of Th and Treg cells within the clusters could secure effective IL-2 delivery for Treg cells even if IL-2 is released in a non-directional manner.
source: The reduction of motility of Th and Treg cells within the clusters could secure effective IL-2 delivery for Treg cells even if IL-2 is released in a non-directional manner.
evidence: Inference about mechanism of IL-2 delivery in cell clusters

claim: Chinen et al. proved the essential role of IL-2R-dependent activation of STAT5 in controlling suppressor function of mature Treg cells.
source: Most recently, Chinen et al. proved the essential role of IL-2R-dependent activation of STAT5 in controlling suppressor function of mature Treg cells (Chinen et al., 2016).
evidence: Citation to prior work by Chinen et al., 2016

claim: Augmented STAT5 activation in differentiated Treg cells increases the formation of Treg-DC-cell-conjugates and potentiates suppressor function in a TCR-independent manner.
source: Using genetic gain and loss of function approaches they demonstrated that augmented STAT5 activation in differentiated Treg cells increases the formation of Treg-DC-cell-conjugates and potentiates suppressor function in a TCR-independent manner.
evidence: Citation to findings by Chinen et al., 2016

claim: There are substantial differences between in vitro and in vivo experimental data concerning IL-2 and CD25 expression and regulation.
source: In summary, we have shown that there are substantial differences between in vitro and in vivo experimental data concerning IL-2 and CD25 expression and regulation.
evidence: Summary conclusion from comparison of in vitro and in vivo data

claim: Computational modeling serves as a valuable and indispensable tool to understand complex regulatory mechanisms in vivo.
source: Furthermore, we have demonstrated that computational modeling serves as a valuable and indispensable tool to understand complex regulatory mechanisms in vivo.
evidence: Conclusion about the utility of computational modeling
